incidents.name: Lumi Finance paymaster approval drain
incidents.notes: Sodium wallet validation accepted an unauthorized session key and then approved an attacker-supplied paymaster's requested token allowance, enabling the paymaster to drain Lumi users' tokens.

sources.ref: verified Sodium implementation deployed by 0x0f369f61983cb0c4a432e4a81aaaa24f2d48be45 in tx 0x259d0c343896630f0a94cd7d4ff69fd489d424618368aa362a37b9662e21cce4; the attack transaction's destination was attacker infrastructure

deployment-basis recheck: the verified Sodium implementation's runtime is byte-identical at the creation block 142595379 and the incident block 483389834, and it holds no EIP-1967, beacon or low storage slot. callTracer shows it is never the caller of a DELEGATECALL in the attack - it is the callee, executed in the context of the wallet proxies (e.g. 0x0209d8fcb0c36399eb49e018a245c55fd37d16bd DELEGATECALLs into it with validateUserOp 0x3a871cdd). Its own two delegatecall sites are OpenZeppelin Address.functionDelegateCall and the caller-supplied Enum.Operation.DelegateCall branch of executeTransaction, neither of which can repoint the contract's own code. Deployment is exact; 996.0 days.
